lessons.title: Notre année scientifique en révision
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify and recall the main science topics they explored during the year

opening.activity: Welcome circle and year overview introduction
opening.visualSupports: Timeline display of the school year with science unit photos

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves semblent nerveux ou timides au début?
decisionPoints.ifYes: utiliser des jeux de brise-glace et rassurer sur l'aspect amusant de partager
decisionPoints.ifNo: procéder avec enthousiasme à l'introduction de la révision

main.activity: Interactive science year review using timeline and memory sharing
main.visualSupports: Visual timeline with unit icons and key vocabulary cards

decisionPoints.question: What science topics were most memorable for students this year?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on those topics for deeper recall and connection
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use visual prompts and peer sharing to activate memories

decisionPoints.question: Should we use a timeline format or topic-by-topic review?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Continue with chronological timeline approach
decisionPoints.ifNo: Switch to thematic groupings of similar concepts

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to make connections between different science units?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Guide students to find links between units
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on individual unit recall before making connections

closing.activity: Share one favorite science memory with the class

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves ont de la difficulté à se rappeler leurs expériences scientifiques?
decisionPoints.ifYes: utiliser plus d'indices visuels et permettre de regarder dans leurs cahiers
decisionPoints.ifNo: encourager le partage plus détaillé et les connexions entre sujets

decisionPoints.question: Le temps est-il suffisant pour que tous partagent leur souvenir préféré?
decisionPoints.ifYes: permettre à chacun de partager brièvement
decisionPoints.ifNo: faire partager en paires puis quelques volontaires avec la classe

troubleshooting.then: use visual prompts, peer partnerships, and journal browsing to support recall

lessons.realWorldConnection: Reflecting on learning helps us understand how much we've grown, like looking at photos from the beginning of the year

forStruggling: Provide picture cards showing different science activities to help trigger memories
Allow students to work with a partner to recall science experiences together
Use simple yes/no questions about science topics rather than open-ended recall
forAdvanced: Encourage students to make connections between different science units they studied
Ask students to identify their favorite science concept and explain why it was interesting
Challenge students to think about science questions they still wonder about
forELL: Provide visual vocabulary cards with science terms in both French and home language
Use gestures and actions when reviewing different science activities
Allow students to draw their science memories instead of only using words
forIEP: Break the review into smaller chunks with breaks between topics
Provide a visual schedule showing the order of science units reviewed
Use concrete objects from science activities to help trigger specific memories

observable: Student can name at least 2 science topics studied during the year
Student can describe one specific science activity or discovery they remember
Student participates actively in timeline discussions and memory sharing
Student uses appropriate science vocabulary when describing past experiences
checkpoints: Opening circle: Does student show recognition when science topics are mentioned?
Timeline activity: Can student point to or identify familiar science unit images?
Memory sharing: Does student contribute to discussion with specific science memories?
Closing: Can student name one favorite science experience from the year?

lessons.title: Nos découvertes les plus excitantes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify their most exciting scientific discoveries from the year and explain why they were special

opening.activity: Review previous lesson and introduce the concept of scientific discoveries
opening.visualSupports: Images of famous scientific discoveries adapted for Grade 1

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves confondent découverte avec invention?
decisionPoints.ifYes: clarifier avec des exemples simples : découvrir = trouver ce qui existe déjà
decisionPoints.ifNo: approfondir leur compréhension des découvertes scientifiques

main.activity: Individual reflection and small group sharing of most exciting science discoveries
main.visualSupports: Sentence starters and emotion words display

decisionPoints.question: Should students share discoveries individually or in small groups?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use individual presentation format with audience
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep to small group sharing for comfort and time management

decisionPoints.question: How can we help students who struggle to identify favorite discoveries?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide guided prompts and visual reminders of activities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use peer partnerships to help generate ideas together

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to explain their thinking or should we focus on sharing experiences?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include 'why' questions in sharing prompts
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on describing what happened and how it felt

closing.activity: Gallery walk of discovery drawings with positive comments

decisionPoints.question: Tous les élèves ont-ils identifié au moins une découverte à partager?
decisionPoints.ifYes: célébrer leurs choix et commencer la planification
decisionPoints.ifNo: offrir du soutien individuel pour identifier une découverte simple

decisionPoints.question: Le niveau d'excitation est-il approprié ou trop élevé?
decisionPoints.ifYes: canaliser l'énergie vers la planification de demain
decisionPoints.ifNo: utiliser des activités calmantes pour terminer positivement

troubleshooting.then: encourage choosing one for now and saving others for later lessons

lessons.realWorldConnection: Scientists often share their most exciting discoveries with others, just like we share exciting news with friends

forStruggling: Provide a choice between 2-3 specific discoveries with visual reminders
Allow students to point to pictures instead of describing with words
Use partner support to help recall and share discovery experiences
forAdvanced: Encourage students to explain WHY their discovery was exciting using science reasoning
Ask students to connect their discovery to how it relates to the real world
Challenge students to think about what questions their discovery raised for them
forELL: Provide discovery vocabulary cards with visual supports
Allow students to use gestures and demonstrations alongside French words
Offer sentence frames: 'Ma découverte préférée était...' 'C'était excitant parce que...'
forIEP: Pre-select 2-3 appropriate discoveries for students to choose from
Use concrete materials from past activities to help recall experiences
Allow alternative ways to show excitement (drawing, acting, simple words)

observable: Student can identify one specific scientific discovery they found exciting
Student can explain using simple words why the discovery was special to them
Student uses appropriate emotion vocabulary (excitant, spécial, fantastique)
Student shares discovery experience with enthusiasm and engagement
checkpoints: Discovery reflection: Can student choose one discovery to focus on?
Small group sharing: Does student communicate excitement about their discovery?
Drawing activity: Does student's drawing show details about their discovery?
Gallery walk: Does student respond positively to others' discoveries?

lessons.title: Qu'est-ce qu'une exposition scientifique?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand what a science fair or exposition is and how scientists share their work

opening.activity: Connect sharing discoveries to the idea of science exhibitions
opening.visualSupports: Age-appropriate images of children at science fairs and exhibitions

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves confondent exposition scientifique avec spectacle de talents?
decisionPoints.ifYes: clarifier qu'on montre ce qu'on a appris en sciences, pas un talent
decisionPoints.ifNo: approfondir leur compréhension du partage scientifique

main.activity: Explore the concept of science sharing through videos, pictures, and role-play
main.visualSupports: Simple flowchart showing: Learn → Practice → Share → Celebrate

decisionPoints.question: Should we show examples of science fairs or focus on simple sharing concepts?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use carefully selected, age-appropriate science fair videos
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on familiar sharing experiences like show-and-tell

decisionPoints.question: How can we make the concept accessible without overwhelming students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use simple analogies and familiar sharing situations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Break down the concept into very small, concrete steps

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to understand audience or should we focus on showing work?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include discussion about who comes to see science work
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus mainly on the act of showing what we've learned

closing.activity: Practice being a science audience for teacher demonstration

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves comprennent-ils bien le concept d'exposition?
decisionPoints.ifYes: passer à pratiquer d'être un bon public
decisionPoints.ifNo: donner plus d'exemples concrets et familiers

decisionPoints.question: Certains élèves semblent-ils inquiets de présenter devant d'autres?
decisionPoints.ifYes: rassurer que c'est normal et qu'on va pratiquer beaucoup ensemble
decisionPoints.ifNo: célébrer leur confiance et les encourager à aider leurs pairs

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: understanding the concept of formal presentation
troubleshooting.then: relate to familiar experiences like birthday parties or school concerts

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how people share their best work at art shows, school concerts, or sports games

forStruggling: Focus on familiar sharing experiences like show-and-tell or sharing toys
Use concrete examples: 'showing your drawings to grandparents' instead of abstract concepts
Provide simple picture cards showing different ways people share their work
forAdvanced: Introduce the idea that scientists share discoveries to help other people learn
Discuss different ways scientists share their work (books, videos, teaching)
Connect science sharing to how students can teach others what they've learned
forELL: Use visual supports showing: montrer (show), partager (share), exposition (display)
Practice key vocabulary with gestures and real examples in the classroom
Allow students to connect concept to sharing traditions from their home culture
forIEP: Break the concept into single steps: Learn something → Show it to others
Use role-play with concrete props rather than discussing abstract concepts
Focus on the celebration aspect of sharing rather than formal presentation

observable: Student can describe what an exposition or science fair is in simple terms
Student understands that an exposition is about sharing what we've learned
Student connects exposition concept to familiar sharing experiences
Student shows interest in the idea of sharing their own science learning
checkpoints: Role-play activity: Does student participate appropriately as audience member?
Discussion: Can student give examples of times when people share their work?
Video viewing: Does student make connections between videos and their own experiences?
Closing practice: Does student demonstrate good audience behaviors?

lessons.title: Choisir notre projet de démonstration
lessons.oneGoal: Students will select one science topic or experiment from the year to demonstrate at the exposition

opening.activity: Review science year and introduce project selection
opening.visualSupports: Visual menu of science topics studied this year with pictures

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves ont trop d'idées et n'arrivent pas à choisir?
decisionPoints.ifYes: les aider à identifier leurs 2-3 découvertes les plus importantes
decisionPoints.ifNo: les encourager à réfléchir plus profondément à leurs expériences

main.activity: Individual reflection and selection process with teacher conferences
main.visualSupports: Decision-making criteria poster: Safe, Fun, I Know It Well

decisionPoints.question: Should students choose individually or work in small groups?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow individual choice with option for partnerships
decisionPoints.ifNo: Organize into predetermined small groups with shared choices

decisionPoints.question: What criteria should guide project selection (interest, success, safety)?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use all three criteria in a simple checklist format
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on student interest and engagement level

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for independent choice or need guided options?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide full menu of year's topics for selection
decisionPoints.ifNo: Pre-select 4-5 most appropriate options for students to choose from

closing.activity: Share chosen project with a partner and explain why

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves arrivent-ils à expliquer leur choix de projet?
decisionPoints.ifYes: encourager des explications plus détaillées avec des raisons
decisionPoints.ifNo: fournir des phrases modèles : 'J'ai choisi... parce que...'

decisionPoints.question: Y a-t-il des élèves qui veulent changer leur choix après avoir écouté les autres?
decisionPoints.ifYes: permettre un changement final si c'est bien réfléchi
decisionPoints.ifNo: confirmer les choix et célébrer la diversité des projets

troubleshooting.then: use elimination process and 'gut feeling' check to narrow choices

lessons.realWorldConnection: Making choices about what to share, like picking our best artwork for a family display

forStruggling: Limit choices to 2-3 pre-selected appropriate science topics
Use visual reminders showing students doing each activity successfully
Provide teacher conference support to talk through each option
forAdvanced: Encourage students to choose topics they can extend or teach in new ways
Allow students to combine two related science topics if appropriate
Challenge students to think about what aspect of their topic was most interesting
forELL: Provide topic cards with both French labels and visual representations
Allow students to discuss choices in partner talk before individual decision
Use simple vocabulary: 'J'aime...', 'Je suis bon à...', 'Je veux montrer...'
forIEP: Pre-select 2 topics that the student had clear success with during the year
Use concrete materials from activities to help recall experiences
Allow selection through pointing, drawing, or simple words rather than complex reasoning

observable: Student can make a choice between science topics based on their interests
Student can give a simple reason for their project choice (fun, good at it, liked it)
Student demonstrates understanding of selection criteria (safe, doable, interesting)
Student shows confidence and enthusiasm about their chosen demonstration topic
checkpoints: Selection process: Does student engage meaningfully with choice-making?
Teacher conference: Can student explain their reasoning for their choice?
Partner sharing: Does student communicate excitement about their chosen project?
Reflection: Does student's choice align with their demonstrated interests and abilities?

lessons.title: Planifier notre démonstration
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a simple plan for how they will show their chosen science topic to visitors

opening.activity: Review chosen projects and introduce planning concepts
opening.visualSupports: Simple planning template with pictures: What? How? What do I need?

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves semblent dépassés par le concept de planification?
decisionPoints.ifYes: simplifier en se concentrant sur une seule étape à la fois
decisionPoints.ifNo: procéder avec l'introduction complète du processus de planification

main.activity: Create individual planning sheets with drawings and simple steps
main.visualSupports: Step-by-step planning process poster and sample completed plans

decisionPoints.question: Should we provide planning templates or encourage creative formats?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide basic template but allow creative additions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with completely open-ended planning approach

decisionPoints.question: How detailed should the planning be for Grade 1 students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include 3-4 simple steps with drawings
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on just the main idea and one key step

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for thinking about audience needs or focus on their own presentation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include 'What will visitors see?' in planning
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on 'What will I do?' for now

closing.activity: Partner sharing of plans with feedback and suggestions

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves ont-ils créé des plans réalistes et réalisables?
decisionPoints.ifYes: célébrer leurs idées et encourager le partage constructif
decisionPoints.ifNo: aider à ajuster les plans pour qu'ils soient plus simples et faisables

decisionPoints.question: Le feedback entre partenaires est-il constructif et encourageant?
decisionPoints.ifYes: modéliser des commentaires encore plus spécifiques et utiles
decisionPoints.ifNo: enseigner des phrases pour donner des commentaires positifs

troubleshooting.then: use think-aloud modeling and break into very small actions

lessons.realWorldConnection: Planning how to explain something to others, like teaching a game to a younger child

forStruggling: Provide a very simple template with pictures: First I will..., Then I will..., Last I will...
Focus on just 2 steps: What I will show and What I will say
Use partner support to help think through the planning process
forAdvanced: Encourage students to think about what questions visitors might ask
Include planning for how to make the demonstration interactive for the audience
Challenge students to plan for different age audiences (other Grade 1s vs. older students)
forELL: Provide planning vocabulary with visual supports: d'abord (first), puis (then), finalement (finally)
Allow drawings with simple French labels instead of full sentences
Use sentence frames: 'Je vais montrer...' 'Les visiteurs vont voir...' 'J'ai besoin de...'
forIEP: Break planning into one step at a time with visual supports for each
Use concrete props to help student physically plan out their demonstration
Focus on the main action: 'I will show...' with support to add details later

observable: Student can create a simple plan with 2-3 steps for their demonstration
Student identifies what materials or props they will need for their presentation
Student can explain their plan to a partner using simple language
Student's plan aligns logically with their chosen science topic
checkpoints: Planning activity: Does student engage with creating steps for their demonstration?
Template completion: Can student fill in planning sheet with appropriate information?
Partner sharing: Does student communicate their plan clearly to others?
Teacher check-in: Is student's plan realistic and doable for their abilities?

lessons.title: Matériel et outils nécessaires
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify and gather the materials they need for their science demonstration

opening.activity: Review plans and introduce material identification
opening.visualSupports: Safety symbol chart and material category pictures

decisionPoints.question: Si certains élèves veulent des matériaux non sécuritaires pour leur démonstration?
decisionPoints.ifYes: explorer des alternatives sécuritaires qui donnent le même effet
decisionPoints.ifNo: célébrer leurs choix sécuritaires et procéder

main.activity: Create material lists and practice safe handling procedures
main.visualSupports: Material safety chart with green, yellow, and red categories

decisionPoints.question: Which materials are safe and appropriate for student-led demonstrations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow all green-category materials with student responsibility
decisionPoints.ifNo: Restrict to pre-approved safe materials list only

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on simple materials or allow more complex tools with supervision?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include some yellow-category materials with adult helper assigned
decisionPoints.ifNo: Stick to simple, completely safe materials students can handle alone

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for material responsibility or need teacher-prepared sets?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have students gather and organize their own materials
decisionPoints.ifNo: Pre-prepare material sets with student input on arrangement

closing.activity: Practice setup and cleanup procedures with materials

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves arrivent-ils à organiser leur matériel efficacement?
decisionPoints.ifYes: chronométrer pour ajouter un défi amusant de vitesse
decisionPoints.ifNo: réduire le nombre de matériaux et pratiquer plus lentement

troubleshooting.then: create visual checklist and practice run-through with materials

lessons.realWorldConnection: Getting ready for activities by gathering what we need, like packing for a trip or preparing for cooking

forStruggling: Provide pre-made material lists specific to each student's chosen demonstration
Use picture cards showing each needed material instead of written lists
Partner students with material organization helpers
forAdvanced: Encourage students to think about backup materials in case something breaks
Include students in making safety decisions about their material choices
Challenge students to organize materials for efficient setup and cleanup
forELL: Provide material vocabulary cards with French labels and pictures
Practice key phrases: 'J'ai besoin de...', 'C'est sécuritaire', 'C'est fragile'
Use hands-on material exploration with vocabulary practice
forIEP: Focus on 3-4 essential materials rather than comprehensive lists
Use concrete materials handling practice before list-making
Provide step-by-step visual sequence for material gathering

observable: Student can identify the main materials needed for their science demonstration
Student demonstrates understanding of material safety categories (safe/needs help)
Student can organize materials in a logical way for their presentation
Student follows appropriate safety procedures when handling demonstration materials
checkpoints: Material listing: Can student identify what they need for their demonstration?
Safety practice: Does student show appropriate caution with different materials?
Organization activity: Can student arrange materials for easy access during demonstration?
Setup practice: Does student demonstrate safe and efficient material handling?

lessons.title: Pratiquer notre explication simple
lessons.oneGoal: Students will practice explaining their science topic using simple words that other children can understand

opening.activity: Warm-up with simple explanation practice using familiar objects
opening.visualSupports: Simple explanation framework: This is... It does... I like it because...

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves utilisent un vocabulaire trop complexe pour leur âge?
decisionPoints.ifYes: modéliser des mots plus simples et faire pratiquer ensemble
decisionPoints.ifNo: encourager leur vocabulaire tout en ajoutant des explications simples

main.activity: Practice rounds with partners, focusing on clear, simple language
main.visualSupports: Word choice helper chart: hard words → easy words

decisionPoints.question: Should students practice with peers or adults first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Start with peer practice for comfort level
decisionPoints.ifNo: Begin with adult practice for immediate feedback

decisionPoints.question: How can we help students use age-appropriate vocabulary?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide word substitution chart and practice
decisionPoints.ifNo: Model simple language and have students repeat

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for feedback on their explanations or need encouragement first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include gentle, specific feedback with encouragement
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus purely on positive reinforcement and building confidence

closing.activity: One-minute explanation challenge with whole group audience

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves sont-ils prêts pour une explication devant tout le groupe?
decisionPoints.ifYes: célébrer leur courage et donner des encouragements spécifiques
decisionPoints.ifNo: garder les groupes plus petits et augmenter graduellement

troubleshooting.then: practice explaining to a stuffed animal or younger child first

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning to explain things clearly so others understand, like telling someone how to play our favorite game

forStruggling: Provide sentence starters: 'D'abord...', 'Puis...', 'C'est important parce que...'
Use props and visual aids to support verbal explanations
Practice with very patient partners who encourage rather than correct
forAdvanced: Encourage students to explain the 'why' behind their science topic, not just the 'what'
Challenge students to think of questions their audience might ask
Practice explaining the same concept in different ways for different audiences
forELL: Allow mixing of gestures, drawing, and simple French words during explanations
Practice key explanation vocabulary with visual supports
Pair with French-speaking partners for modeling and support
forIEP: Focus on explaining just one key point clearly rather than comprehensive explanations
Use concrete objects and hands-on demonstration instead of abstract explanations
Allow alternative communication methods (drawing, pointing, demonstrating)

observable: Student can explain their science topic using vocabulary appropriate for other Grade 1 students
Student includes key information about their topic (what it is, what happens, why it's interesting)
Student speaks clearly and at an appropriate volume for their audience
Student responds positively to gentle feedback and makes adjustments to their explanation
checkpoints: Partner practice: Does student communicate their main idea clearly to peer audience?
Vocabulary use: Does student choose simple, understandable words over complex terms?
Engagement: Does student show enthusiasm while explaining their topic?
Feedback response: Can student incorporate suggestions to improve their explanation?

lessons.title: Créer un affichage visuel
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a simple visual display (drawing, poster, or model) to support their science demonstration

opening.activity: Look at examples of visual displays and discuss their purpose
opening.visualSupports: Gallery of age-appropriate science displays with features highlighted

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves veulent copier exactement les exemples montrés?
decisionPoints.ifYes: encourager l'adaptation des idées plutôt que la copie directe
decisionPoints.ifNo: célébrer leur créativité et leurs idées originales

main.activity: Create individual visual displays with choice of format and materials
main.visualSupports: Visual display planning template and design idea examples

decisionPoints.question: What visual formats are most appropriate for Grade 1 science concepts?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow choice between drawing, simple poster, or basic model
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on drawings with labels as the primary format

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on drawings, simple posters, or 3D models?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Offer all three options based on student project needs
decisionPoints.ifNo: Standardize on one format for consistency and time management

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for independent creation or need guided templates?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide optional templates but encourage creative additions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use structured templates with specific areas for student input

closing.activity: Gallery walk with positive feedback on visual displays

decisionPoints.question: Les affichages créés supportent-ils bien les démonstrations scientifiques?
decisionPoints.ifYes: encourager les élèves à expliquer comment ils vont les utiliser
decisionPoints.ifNo: aider à identifier un élément clé à ajouter ou modifier

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: knowing what to include in display
troubleshooting.then: use guiding questions: What? How? Why is it cool?

lessons.realWorldConnection: Using pictures and displays to help explain ideas, like showing photos when telling about vacation

forStruggling: Provide simple templates or pre-drawn outlines for visual displays
Focus on one key concept rather than comprehensive displays
Use partner support for planning and organizing visual elements
forAdvanced: Encourage students to create interactive elements for their visual display
Include multiple ways to show the same concept (drawing, diagram, model)
Challenge students to design displays that teach others step-by-step
forELL: Use visual vocabulary cards with French labels for display creation
Allow combination of drawings and simple French words/phrases
Practice key vocabulary: 'affichage', 'montrer', 'expliquer', 'intéressant'
forIEP: Focus on creating one clear visual element rather than complex displays
Use concrete materials and hands-on creation over abstract planning
Provide step-by-step visual guides for display creation process

observable: Student creates a visual display that supports their science demonstration
Student includes key information about their science topic in visual format
Student uses appropriate materials and organization in their display
Student can explain how their visual display helps others understand their topic
checkpoints: Planning phase: Does student identify key elements to include in their display?
Creation phase: Does student work purposefully to create meaningful visual supports?
Review phase: Can student explain how their display connects to their demonstration?
Integration phase: Does student see how visual and verbal elements work together?

lessons.title: Questions que les visiteurs pourraient poser
lessons.oneGoal: Students will anticipate and practice answering simple questions about their science topic

opening.activity: Introduce the idea of visitor questions through role-play
opening.visualSupports: Common question types poster with picture cues

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves semblent anxieux à l'idée de répondre aux questions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: rassurer que les visiteurs posent des questions parce qu'ils sont intéressés
decisionPoints.ifNo: encourager leur enthousiasme et leur confiance naturelle

main.activity: Generate possible questions and practice answering with partners
main.visualSupports: Answer framework: I think... because... Do you want to see?

decisionPoints.question: What types of questions are most likely from different age groups?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Practice with age-specific question categories
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on general curiosity questions regardless of age

decisionPoints.question: Should we practice specific questions or general question-answering skills?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Create specific question bank for each project type
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on general questioning strategies and comfort building

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for unknown questions or should we stick to predictable ones?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include some surprise questions in practice
decisionPoints.ifNo: Practice only with predictable, prepared questions

closing.activity: Quick question-answer rounds with the whole class as visitors

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves répondent-ils avec confiance aux questions de leurs pairs?
decisionPoints.ifYes: ajouter quelques questions surprises pour développer leur flexibilité
decisionPoints.ifNo: revenir à des questions plus prévisibles et rassurantes

troubleshooting.then: practice saying 'That's a great question! Let me think...' or 'I'm not sure, but I know...'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Being ready to answer questions about things we know well, like explaining our favorite books or toys

forStruggling: Pre-practice with 2-3 simple, predictable questions about their topic
Use visual cue cards to remind students of key answer points
Practice with very supportive peer partners who ask gentle questions
forAdvanced: Encourage students to think of follow-up questions visitors might ask
Practice explaining their topic in different ways if first explanation unclear
Challenge students to connect their topic to visitors' own experiences
forELL: Practice key question-answer vocabulary: 'Qu'est-ce que...?', 'Comment...?', 'Pourquoi...?'
Use sentence frames for answers: 'C'est...', 'Ça marche parce que...', 'J'aime ça parce que...'
Allow use of gestures and props to support verbal answers
forIEP: Focus on understanding and answering just one type of question well
Use concrete examples and hands-on demonstrations rather than abstract explanations
Practice with familiar adults before peer or visitor interactions

observable: Student can anticipate basic questions visitors might ask about their topic
Student provides appropriate answers using simple, clear language
Student responds to questions with confidence and enthusiasm
Student uses their demonstration materials to help answer questions
checkpoints: Question anticipation: Can student predict what others might wonder about their topic?
Answer preparation: Does student practice clear, simple responses?
Interactive practice: Does student engage appropriately during question practice?
Confidence building: Does student show increasing comfort with Q&A format?

lessons.title: Sécurité pendant notre démonstration
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify and practice safety rules for their science demonstration with visitors

opening.activity: Review general safety rules and apply them to demonstration contexts
opening.visualSupports: Safety rules poster with pictures and symbols

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves minimisent l'importance de la sécurité?
decisionPoints.ifYes: utiliser des exemples concrets et des scénarios réalistes
decisionPoints.ifNo: célébrer leur conscience de la sécurité et approfondir

main.activity: Create personalized safety checklists and practice safety procedures
main.visualSupports: Safety action cards: Stop, Look, Think, Ask

decisionPoints.question: Which safety considerations are most important for student-led demonstrations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on material handling and visitor guidance safety
decisionPoints.ifNo: Concentrate on basic personal safety and space organization

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on material safety or visitor safety protocols?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both with emphasis on visitor safety
decisionPoints.ifNo: Prioritize material safety as the foundation

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for safety leadership or need adult supervision reminders?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Practice student safety leadership with backup adult support
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on recognizing when to call for adult help

closing.activity: Safety scenario practice with problem-solving discussions

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves identifient-ils les situations qui nécessitent l'aide d'un adulte?
decisionPoints.ifYes: pratiquer comment demander de l'aide poliment et clairement
decisionPoints.ifNo: donner plus d'exemples concrets de quand appeler à l'aide

troubleshooting.then: create visual safety reminder cards and practice calm breathing

lessons.realWorldConnection: Being responsible for safety when showing others our activities, like teaching someone to ride a bike safely

forStruggling: Focus on 2-3 most important safety rules rather than comprehensive lists
Use visual safety symbols and pictures rather than word-based rules

lessons.title: Apprendre des autres projets
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify interesting ideas and discoveries they learned from other students' demonstrations

opening.activity: Share memories of seeing other students' science projects
opening.visualSupports: Photo gallery of all student projects from the exposition

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves ont de la difficulté à se souvenir des projets des autres?
decisionPoints.ifYes: utiliser les photos pour stimuler les souvenirs
decisionPoints.ifNo: encourager le partage détaillé des observations

main.activity: Structured sharing about what students learned from classmates' projects
main.visualSupports: Learning from others chart and appreciation sentence starters

decisionPoints.question: Should we structure learning observations or allow free exploration?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide guided observation questions with free sharing time
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use completely open sharing about interesting discoveries

decisionPoints.question: How can we help students articulate what they found interesting?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use specific prompts about what surprised or excited them
decisionPoints.ifNo: Allow general sharing of positive reactions and feelings

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for comparing approaches or should we focus on appreciation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include gentle comparisons about different ways to show science
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus purely on appreciation and positive observations

closing.activity: Create thank-you notes or appreciation messages for classmates

decisionPoints.situation: Si un élève ne se souvient d'aucune présentation de ses camarades
decisionPoints.action: utiliser des photos ou supports visuels pour stimuler la mémoire et encourager l'observation

decisionPoints.situation: Si les messages de remerciement deviennent répétitifs ou génériques
decisionPoints.action: guider vers des détails spécifiques appréciés chez chaque camarade

decisionPoints.situation: Si un élève exprime de la jalousie envers le travail d'un autre
decisionPoints.action: rediriger vers l'appréciation de la diversité et comment chacun apporte quelque chose de spécial

troubleshooting.then: use photos and documentation to prompt memories and observations

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning new things from friends and family, discovering that everyone has interesting knowledge to share

forStruggling: Focus on identifying just one interesting thing learned from others' presentations
Use visual supports showing different classmates' topics to help trigger memories
Allow simple expressions of interest: 'J'ai aimé...', 'C'était cool...'
forAdvanced: Encourage students to make connections between different classmates' science topics
Include students in thinking about questions they still have after seeing others' work
Challenge students to identify science topics they'd like to explore further
forELL: Provide vocabulary for expressing interest: intéressant, nouveau, surprenant, cool
Use sentence frames: 'J'ai appris que...', 'Je ne savais pas que...', 'Maintenant je comprends...'
Allow students to draw or point to express their learning from others
forIEP: Focus on concrete, observable things from classmates' presentations
Use photos or materials from other presentations to help recall specific learning
Celebrate the student's attention and interest in others' work

observable: Student can describe something interesting they learned from classmates' science presentations
Student shows appreciation and interest in the variety of science topics explored by peers
Student makes connections between others' topics and their own science experiences
Student demonstrates good listening and learning skills during peer presentations
checkpoints: Peer learning: Can student identify specific things learned from classmates' presentations?
Interest expression: Does student show genuine curiosity about others' science topics?
Connection making: Can student relate others' work to their own experiences or interests?
Respectful engagement: Did student demonstrate good audience skills during peer presentations?

lessons.title: Sciences pour l'été
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify safe science exploration opportunities they can pursue during summer break

opening.activity: Introduce summer science exploration and connect to year's learning
opening.visualSupports: Summer science opportunities poster with seasonal activities

decisionPoints.question: Si les élèves semblent fatigués en fin d'année?
decisionPoints.ifYes: garder l'activité courte et se concentrer sur l'enthousiasme
decisionPoints.ifNo: explorer plus d'idées pour les sciences d'été

main.activity: Brainstorm and plan safe summer science activities with family involvement
main.visualSupports: Safe summer science chart and family activity ideas display

decisionPoints.question: Which summer science activities are safest and most accessible for families?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on observation and simple safe activities requiring minimal materials
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide extensive activity options with clear safety guidelines

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on observation activities or simple experiments?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance observation with very simple, safe experimental activities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Concentrate on observation and discovery activities

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for independent science thinking or need structured suggestions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage independent wondering with family support structure
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide specific, structured activity suggestions to follow

closing.activity: Share summer science plans and final celebration of year's science learning

decisionPoints.situation: Si un élève n'arrive pas à penser à des activités scientifiques pour l'été
decisionPoints.action: connecter aux activités estivales qu'il aime déjà et montrer les aspects scientifiques cachés

decisionPoints.situation: Si les élèves deviennent nostalgiques ou tristes que l'année se termine
decisionPoints.action: célébrer tous les apprentissages acquis et l'excitation de continuer à explorer cet été

decisionPoints.situation: Si un élève s'inquiète d'oublier ses apprentissages scientifiques pendant l'été
decisionPoints.action: rassurer qu'explorer la nature et poser des questions maintient l'esprit scientifique vivant

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: thinking of science activities for summer
troubleshooting.then: connect to favorite activities from the year and seasonal opportunities

lessons.realWorldConnection: Continuing to explore and discover during summer through nature walks, backyard observations, and safe family experiments

forStruggling: Focus on simple, safe science activities available at home (water play, nature observation)
Use picture cards showing safe summer science activities
Connect to familiar summer activities that already have science elements
forAdvanced: Encourage students to plan specific science investigations they could do over summer
Include thinking about questions they want to explore further
Challenge students to consider sharing summer discoveries with family or friends
forELL: Provide summer science vocabulary: été, explorer, découvrir, observer, sécuritaire
Use visual supports showing summer science activities
Practice phrases: 'Cet été je vais...', 'Je peux observer...', 'C'est sécuritaire de...'
forIEP: Focus on very simple, concrete summer activities with science connections
Use familiar summer routines and activities as starting points for science thinking
Emphasize safety and adult supervision for any summer science exploration

observable: Student can identify safe science exploration activities appropriate for summer break
Student shows continued interest in science learning beyond the classroom setting
Student demonstrates understanding of safety considerations for independent science exploration
Student makes connections between formal science learning and everyday summer activities
checkpoints: Activity identification: Can student suggest appropriate summer science activities?
Safety awareness: Does student understand the importance of adult supervision and safe practices?
Interest continuation: Does student show enthusiasm for ongoing science exploration?
Connection making: Can student see science in everyday summer activities and experiences?

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: ""

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en sciences
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
Notre année scientifique en révision, Nos découvertes les plus excitantes, Qu'est-ce qu'une exposition scientifique?, Choisir notre projet de démonstration, Planifier notre démonstration

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Encouragez les questions 'pourquoi' et explorez ensemble les réponses.

N'hésitez pas à me contacter si vous avez des questions ou si vous souhaitez partager des ressources culturelles liées à cette unité.

La curiosité scientifique commence à la maison!

Cordialement,
[Nom de l'enseignant(e)]
